Sarah / Acme team —

Thanks for the quick turn on the order form. Attachment: MSA_Redline_v3.docx contains our suggested language. High level proposal below to make progress on liability cap and carve-outs:

- Proposal A (preferred by Redwood): Aggregate cap = greater of (1x billed fees in prior 12 months) OR $3,000,000. No per-claim separate cap.
- Proposal B (alternative for multi-year): Annual reset — cap equals greater of (1x fees billed in that 12-month period) or $1,500,000 per 12-mo period (re-sets each year).

Carve-outs we can accept (i.e., excluded from cap):
- IP indemnity and third-party IP claims;
- Willful misconduct or gross negligence;
- Breach of confidentiality causing regulatory notice;
- Claims arising from Redwood’s breach of data security obligations (with threshold language).

We are proposing to exclude consequential damages generally, but make exceptions where warranted: statutory fines or penalties (e.g., GDPR/CPRA fines) and IP claims. We cannot accept open-ended consequential liability for business interruption beyond the proposed cap.

Rationale: an annual reset is acceptable for long-duration enterprise commitments if Acme wants predictable yearly protection; Redwood prefers a single aggregate cap where possible (simpler for accounting and risk transfer).

Can you confirm Acme’s openness to Proposal A vs Proposal B? If you need numeric movement, our flexibility is +/- 25% on the dollar cap (i.e., $2.25M–$3.75M) depending on the carve-outs accepted.

I’ve CC’d Laura and Priyom from Contracts and Neha on Security so we have alignment on redline language. I attached a redline that implements Proposal A and an alternative section that shows the annual-reset variant.

Proposed next step: 30-min call Wed 3/9 to align legal and procurement, then copy final redline to your counsel for sign-off.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the note and the redline. A few immediate items from Acme Legal’s side: we are generally supportive of a cap, but we need a higher floor given the size of the relationship. Our counter is: aggregate cap = greater of (2x annual fees) OR $6,000,000.

On carve-outs: we need consequential damages to remain available for certain supply-chain and integration failures that cause downstream losses — specifically where Redwood’s failure causes material disruption to our customer-facing systems. IP indemnity carve-out is fine.

Two asks:
1) please provide two concrete examples (one breach scenario, one performance outage) and show how the cap would apply;
2) remove the unilateral language that shifts regulatory fines solely to Acme; we want shared responsibility if Redwood materially contributed to a regulatory event.

We can do a quick sync Wed.
